draft_chronology.reason: The frozen parser treated a colon after any citation as a Markdown reference definition, without considering whether the citation began a line. This is ordinary inline punctuation and a false positive. No claim support was judged for this draft.

The outline-heading claim was rejected as unsupported because S2 contained only the introduction; read_page action3 actually returned the section outline to the planner, but it was omitted from Session.evidence and the auditor payload. The stated existence of the context-manager and manual-start/end headings was supported navigation metadata. The separate claim about no SDK/network in the execution container lacked supplied runtime/code-run evidence and was also rejected.
Removed both optional claims; no further search/read calls occurred between drafts. The answer still contains the useful tracing outline and condensed example.

remaining_caveats: The code names undefined MODEL/client/tool_schema/my_tool/questions, omits assistant/tool message appends and the final model call/return. This is disclosed as condensed, but a beginner needs the full source to run it. It should not be described as a complete working multi-turn agent.

The sentence Each of these emits an OpenTelemetry span follows a list including conversation. Read literally it overstates the hierarchy: S2 explicitly says every turn, LLM call and tool call emits a span; installed Conversation groups by conversation_id and has no span. This is ambiguous wording, not an invented tracing API.
Extra raw-OTel and framework integration alternatives are sourced but distract from the hand-written Python question. They increase length and the surface for verification mistakes.
No live SDK example was executed during this manual review; signature compatibility and Python parsing are narrower checks.

criteria.evidence: Final answer distinguishes grouping from restoring model history and recommends handling history in the application. Installed Conversation stores a ContextVar and ID/defaults; it does not load messages from a database or reconstruct model history.

criteria.evidence: S10 provides exact conversation signature and get_current_conversation behavior; S12 shows conversation.conversation_id. Same agent_name is framed as a recommendation, not the grouping key.

draft_chronology.reason: An unnecessary legacy Threads/Calls comparison had no cited passage. The unqualified history-restoration statement had no source ID and was classified as a partial product claim, triggering the nonempty-source rule. Core ID-reuse guidance was supported.
Removed the legacy aside and reframed history restoration as the limit of the passages plus an application recommendation. No extra retrieval occurred between drafts.

remaining_caveats: The final caveat about processes and long gaps is more hesitant than the task requires: S10 expressly says reuse a stable ID to add turns to an existing conversation. It should not be read as requiring the same Python Conversation object or same process.

ID reuse groups exported traces; authentication, tenant-safe ownership of the app chat ID and durable model-history storage remain application concerns. The answer does not promise those capabilities.
The follow-up includes no init call in its sketch, but the immediately preceding answer established initialization. This is appropriate retained context, not a stand-alone complete setup recipe.
